text: dsh-journal 是面向 DeepSeek Harness 的本机长期日志工具，通过注册 journal 工具，把分级记忆保存为 JSONL 文件。它支持按 S、A、B、C 级添加条目，按关键词搜索和筛选日志，生成 S/A 长期摘要，查看统计并续期条目，也能将过期内容归档或整理成 JOURNAL.md。适合希望在不同会话间保留偏好、决定、项目进度或交接记录的用户。数据默认保存在本机日志目录，可用 JOURNAL_ROOT 指定路径；代码未配置外部服务或 API 密钥。

dsh-journal adds a local journal tool to DSH. It stores graded notes in JSONL and supports keyword search, S/A digests, review, expiry pruning and Markdown rendering. Keep preferences and project notes across sessions. JOURNAL_ROOT sets the path; no API key or external service is declared.
想给 DSH 加一个能按重要程度自动设定保留期限的长期笔记工具。
怎么把跨会话的偏好和项目进度记下来，还能之后按关键词找回？
I need a local journal tool that keeps important notes across sessions and lets me search them by keyword.
dsh-journal 的功能「分级长期日志」：通过 journal 工具添加 S、A、B、C 四级条目，各级按规则设置不同保留期限；支持筛选、关键词搜索、生成长期摘要、续期、整理文档和归档过期记录。

dsh-journal README · dsh-journal：A DeepSeek Harness plugin that turns a plain JSONL file into a first-class `journal` tool with graded memory: entries carry a level, an expiry, and a review date, so a long-lived assistant can remember the right things for the right amount of time — and let the rest go on its own.

dsh-journal README · Why memory needs levels：A single undifferentiated memory file fails in two directions at once. Keep everything and the useful part drowns; keep only recent things and the relationship and the standing preferences — the parts that make an assistant feel like the same person — are exactly what gets dropped.

So every entry gets one of four levels, and the level decides its lifetime:

dsh-journal README · Why memory needs levels：| level | meaning | lifetime |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `S` | relationship, emotion, shared experience, promises | never auto-deleted; pinned |
| `A` | durable facts, preferences, key decisions | 365 days |
| `B` | project context, task progress | 60 days |
| `C` | transient details, one-off operations | 7 days |

`prune` soft-deletes expired rows into `archive/`; nothing is ever physically removed by the tool. Pinned rows are exempt.

dsh-journal README · Why memory needs levels：The useful question when writing is not "is this important" but **"which of these is this, a skeleton or a file"** — the rules for how someone talks to you belong in `S`, the port number you debugged yesterday belongs in `B`, and a handoff note for the next session belongs in `A` because it only needs to survive until you read it.

dsh-journal README · The tool：| action | does |
| --- | --- |
| `add` | write one entry (`level`, `title`, `text` required) |
| `list` | list entries, optionally by level / status |
| `search` | substring search across title, text and tags |
| `digest` | the `S` + `A` summary — what a fresh session should read first |
| `stats` | counts per level, size, expired-but-present |
| `review` | push one entry's expiry out |
| `prune` | soft-delete everything past its expiry |
| `render` | rewrite `JOURNAL.md` as a readable digest |

dsh-journal README · The tool：Typical use in an agent loop:

```
journal action=digest                          # at the start of every new conversation
journal action=add level=S title="..." text="..."
journal action=search query=备考
journal action=prune dryRun=true               # see what would expire, change nothing

dsh-journal README · Storage：One JSON object per line at `<root>/journal.jsonl`. Writes go through a temp file and a rename, so a crash mid-write cannot tear the store. A torn trailing line on read is skipped rather than failing the call.

Row shape:

```json
{
  "id": "j-20261104-140902-479d",
  "ts": "2026-11-04T14:09:02+00:00",
  "level": "B",

The format is deliberately plain. Any script that can read JSONL can read this, and any script that can write one line can add to it.

dsh-journal README · Install：A DeepSeek Harness plugin only receives the host packages (`@deepseek-ai/*`) when it is installed as a **link**. An ordinary npm dependency fails to import and is silently skipped.

Configuration (in the bundle layer `cordis.patch.yml`):

| key | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `root` | `D:/dsh-data/journal` (Windows) / `/dsh-data/journal` | where `journal.jsonl` lives |
| `toolName` | `journal` | the tool's name in the model's toolset |

`JOURNAL_ROOT` overrides `root` from the environment.

dsh-journal README · Test：```bash
node _selftest.mjs
```

Runs against a temporary store: add at each level, list, search, digest, stats, prune dry-run, render, review, and the two validation paths (bad level, empty title are both rejected).

dsh-journal README · Note on what it is not：This is not a vector store and does not do retrieval by similarity. It is a small, inspectable, hand-curated log — closer to a notebook than a database. The bet is that an assistant which writes down the right few hundred lines, and forgets the rest on schedule, beats one that hoards everything and searches it.
